page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-16 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration belonging to the first-generation N1 general purpose compute family. It delivers 16 vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance offers dedicated CPU resource allocation with multithreading enabled at two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 104.0 GB, yielding an elevated allocation of 6.5 GB of system RAM per virtual core. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.25 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, whereas modern AVX-512 extensions and AMX accelerators are not present.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallelized throughput over raw per-core execution speed. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1113.69, rank in the lower quartile of assessed machines. File compression benchmarks further reflect single-thread constraints, registering lower-tier results in gzip and bzip3 tasks. Conversely, parallel metrics perform within the median range, shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5935.0, a PassMark CPU rating of 12812.02, and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 81.5 GB/sec.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external persistent disks for primary data persistence and operating systems. Network throughput supports static web serving at 9.64 GB/sec, while in-memory operations register 10.99 million Redis SET operations per second. Smaller language model evaluations (135M) yield text generation throughput of 165.21 tokens per second, but performance decelerates to 10.38 tokens per second on 7B models. These operational tradeoffs establish n1-highmem-16 as an efficient match for memory-heavy enterprise software, relational database management, medium-scale in-memory caching tiers, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines that prioritize total memory footprint over peak per-thread execution speed.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-16 provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.3 GHz, coupled with 104.0 GB of system memory, delivering 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features AVX and AES instructions alongside a 45 MB L3 cache, while omitting AVX-512 capabilities, GPUs, and integrated local storage. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate moderate multi-core throughput, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 12812.02 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5935.0, contrasting with weaker single-core compute and data compression numbers. Memory throughput achieves 81.5 GB/sec during large-block uncached read workloads, supporting up to 10.99 million Redis SET operations per second. This hardware profile is appropriate for memory-demanding enterprise deployments, relational databases, distributed caching layers, and parallel data transformations requiring substantial RAM capacity.
